title: Chapter 47: Rem
content:
Chapter 47:

Rem

※※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※

—Rem still deeply remembers the emotions she felt at that time.

A swung sword, scattering fresh blood.

The familiar scenery roasted by flames, familiar people turning into silent corpses.

A world coming to an end. A world that had been closed off. An unrewarded world.

A world that was simply harsh, simply unreasonable, where one was simply hurt.

Reaching out a hand, moving fingers, trembling lips, and still pleading.

Even if it was such an unsalvageable world, it was all she had.

A world she had only ever peeked at from behind the back that always, always shielded her view.

That wall was suddenly removed, and she squinted at the blinding glare of the expanded world, searing the heat and color of the skin-burning flames, the stench and color of scorching flesh, the beauty and color of the “horn” dancing in the air—searing everything into her eyes, into a field of vision that hadn’t even fully opened—.

In a world that might already be ending, what was she thinking?

The emotion she acquired in that moment—because she still remembers it now.

Every day of her life since then has been made up solely of atonement for that emotion.

※※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※

—For the girl named Rem, being compared to her sister had been a highly painful daily reality.

Among demi-humans, the physical strength and mana possessed by the Oni clan fell into an exceptionally high class.

Their unparalleled combat prowess and their racial trait as the “Kings of the Forest” further strengthened their superiority in nature, displaying enough power to have their existence recognized as one of the strongest among demi-humans.

The toughness of their bodies, the quality of the mana they could wield—there was no race more reliable in combat.

If there was a single weakness the Oni clan possessed, it was the low absolute number of their species.

The species specialized in producing mighty individuals did not end up breathing life into many sprouts, and in stark contrast to their power, the Oni clan was forced to live modestly, forming small settlements deep in the mountains.

However, unlike their physical toughness, many of them had gentle temperaments, so not many harbored dissatisfaction with that lifestyle.

Precisely because they were a race living in a land isolated from human habitation, there existed a number of strict laws.

Breaking the law brought punishment, and at worst, even banishment was unavoidable. For them, who huddled together due to their small population, banishment meant a lifetime of solitude.

Therefore, the laws had to be obeyed, no matter what.

—To the Oni clan, twins were “abominations.”

That, too, was one of the strict laws established among the few remaining Oni.

By nature, those of the Oni clan were born possessing two horns on their heads.

In times of peace, their horns were hidden within the skull, but if the situation changed into one that shook their instincts as an Oni, the horns reveal themselves from the head and devour all the surrounding mana.

By subjugating the mana in the atmosphere and bending it to their will, they vastly increased their combat power. The horns were organs for that very purpose, and for the Oni clan, they could be considered the very pride of their species.

And twins, of all things, were born sharing those two horns between them.

Among the Oni, one who had lost their horns was called “Hornless” and lost their standing within the race. Even the loss of a single horn could not escape that stigma. And yet, twins were born lacking those precious horns from the very beginning. How could this be anything but an abomination?

Thus, twins were deemed abominations, and it was customary for them to be disposed of immediately after birth.

Their fate, too, should normally have run out right then and there.

Had the immense magic power emitted by one half of the twins not been discovered at the very moment the execution was to be carried out by the hands of the chieftain who made the bitter decision—if that innate talent had gone unnoticed.

The twins were named Ram for the elder sister and Rem for the younger, and they were permitted to leave their names at the very bottom of the Oni clan.

Their life could by no means be called smooth sailing.

Even though their lives were saved, the fact that they were twins could not be erased.

Branded with the label of “Hornless” from the start, they grew up being treated coldly by everyone in the clan, their parents included.

Their parents never broke their distant attitude despite being bound by blood. Their fellow clansmen hid neither their disgust nor their contempt for the two abominations. For them, who could not yet walk and understood neither words nor malice, it could be said to be the worst possible environment to be raised in.

However, as for how long that life in such a poor environment lasted, it was only until they became aware of their surroundings—more accurately, until the elder twin sister established her self-awareness.

To describe Ram in her infancy, the simplest word would be “prodigy.”

A brilliance unrivaled even among all the Oni clan of past generations. At such a young age, the pool of mana she could wield was exceptionally massive, and above all, the beauty of her horn captivated all the Oni.

Not drowning in her own talent or power, and presenting herself as straight and true as the single pure white horn resting on her forehead, every member of the clan naturally bowed their heads to her figure.

For a girl not even ten years old, it was truly special treatment.

The parents who had been distant, the clansmen who hadn’t hidden their mockery, even the chieftain who had tried to kill them right after birth—all were left speechless before her majesty.

The Oni clan, chosen even among the powerful demi-human races, and an existence born to stand at the apex of those Oni.

Because they revered mighty individuals, they never failed to show the utmost respect to those who are mighty. Precisely that the Oni Clan was such, there was no ulterior motive whatsoever in their devotion to Ram.

Following along the path of such a sister’s glory with merely clumsy steps was Rem’s everyday life.

She had no outstanding talent. The amount of mana she could handle was mediocre. Her power as an Oni was average for someone with a single horn. Unlike her sister, she didn’t have a shred of confidence; she shrank behind her sister’s back, acting as a shadow so as never to catch anyone’s eye or become a topic of conversation.

That was the young girl’s way of surviving the world, and her defense mechanism to protect her underdeveloped heart.

It wasn’t that she was jealous of her sister.

It wasn’t that she hated her parents.

It wasn’t that she found her fellow clansmen a nuisance.

Her sister, who always walked ahead, was unfailingly kind, looking back time and time again to reach out a hand to her slower-walking younger sister.

Her parents, who had been distant, also came to pour equal affection upon her younger sister, Rem, as they came to know the elder sister’s natural gifts.

Not a few of the clansmen in the village also directed eyes of expectation and envy at her as she desperately followed behind her exceptionally brilliant sister.

A sister kinder than anyone else. Parents who placed their expectations on her. All the fellow clansmen who cheered her on to become splendid like her sister—all of it was an agonizing ordeal for Rem, as if her body were being sliced to ribbons.

The fact that she happened to look exactly like her sister, like two peas in a pod, probably had no small effect.

Even though their appearances, down to their height and facial features, were so similar, only their qualities as an “Oni” housed within their bodies differed vastly.

Of course, Rem also made efforts to change that situation.

Though it was nothing more than the shallow, childish trial and error of a young kid, Rem tried every possible means to get even one step closer to her sister, striving to surpass her in at least one thing.

However, in every single aspect, her sister remained above her.

The fact that there was a realm she could never reach no matter what she did, and that the one dwelling in it was the person closest to her and dearer to her than anyone else—Rem was forced to realize this while still in her early childhood.

She could not stand alongside her sister.

Her sister, who always stood in front, bathing first in the light that illuminated the world. Fearfully peeking her face out from behind her sister’s back, shrinking her body under that blinding radiance—that was her place.

By giving up like that, she was able to accept all her daily hardships, just as plants and trees let the wind blow past them.

—Just how long did those days of accepting such resignation last?

※※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※

One night, Rem woke up feeling uncomfortable from the heat.

Lying on her wooden bed, she peeled the blanket off her sweaty body. Looking around, she suddenly realized that her sister, who should have been sleeping in the adjacent bed, was nowhere to be seen.

She immediately thought she had to go look for her sister.

If she was awake, Rem had to follow behind her majestic strides. Even if it was merely a temporary awakening for a bathroom break, the obsession that she must not fail to do so dominated Rem at this time.

Leave the room

—when she thought that, she finally realized, though much too late.

The cause of the heat: the home she was so used to living in was engulfed in flames.

Letting go of the hot doorknob she had touched, Rem arrived at that fact. Her dormant sense of smell awoke, detecting the burning stench, and an itch ran across her forehead as her horn pushed its way to the surface.

Instantly, she smashed through the door with her enhanced body, dashing through the house veiled in hellfire. She didn’t know the reason. But she ran outward, outward, just as her instincts commanded.

Destroying a weakened wall with a single kick, Rem burst out of the house.

Even in this moment, what dominated her mind was a sort of fanatic thought: “Rem must get outside and seek her sister’s instructions.”

That thought was overwritten in an instant by the scene she witnessed outside the house.

The center of the settlement. There lay a mountain of charred corpses piled high.

Blazing homes; scorched trees; the familiar world had turned into a red hell in a single night.

Seeing familiar faces lined up among the twisted corpses roasted by the flames, Rem instantly abandoned all thought and collapsed on the spot.

Figures draped in black robes slowly surrounded her. The faces of the deeply hooded shadows couldn’t be seen until they were close, and she didn’t recognize the faces she did see. However, she couldn’t sense any friendly light in them at all, and Rem’s cheeks floated an unfitting smile.

It was a face too philosophical for a young girl to make, a face that had bitten back resignation over and over.

The shadows paid not the slightest heed to that expression, which was even accompanied by a sense of pathos.

Raising their hands, they swung down the silver blades gleaming in their palms toward the girl—immediately after, the heads of the shadows flew off all at once.

Fresh blood. Four lives taken simultaneously, their flying heads a testament to a skill so brilliant they didn’t even realize their own demise; not even a scream was raised.

Feeling that familiar wave of mana directly against her skin, Rem was certain it was her sister’s doing.

The moment she perceived that, Rem stood up on the spot.

If her sister was somewhere nearby, she had to follow behind her back.

There was no need to cast her gaze around; she found her figure right away.

Her face, identical to Rem’s own, was now twisted in tragic grief as she ran up to her younger sister and embraced her. Checking that there were no wounds on Rem’s body in her arms, her body relaxed in relief.

Hugging that body back, Rem chewed on the utmost happiness and sorrow.

—What happened after that, she didn’t remember well.

She supposed she just left everything to her sister.

That was the best, and above all, correct. Because whatever her sister did was always the most esteemed choice among all possibilities.

And yet, by the time she noticed, they were surrounded on all sides.

The number of silhouettes was enough to completely cover her field of vision, and while vaguely staring at them, Rem still completely believed her sister would somehow handle it.

The back right in front of her was desperately screaming something.

Shedding tears, shrinking her body, frantically pleading something.

When she was forced to the ground, Rem was troubled. Because looking down at her sister was a situation that absolutely must not happen in her way of living.

Behind her sister, making herself smaller than her sister—doing so was her reason for existing.

Her sister screamed. Standing up, spreading both hands in front of her.

Mana surged. Her sister’s abnormal power was deployed, and invisible blades that sliced everything in the surroundings to pieces trampled the world.

But before that rushed out, her sister turned back and embraced Rem—an impact.

And then, Rem saw it.

A piece of steel struck the side of her sister’s head, sending that white radiance dancing into the red sky.

Round and round and round, the severed horn spun.

The horn severed from its base, the spurting fresh blood, and someone’s high-pitched scream.

What she thought upon witnessing that, she remembered vividly even now.

While listening to the screams of her beloved sister, who had protected her, suffered assault, and had her horn broken off, and while watching that beautiful white horn she had endlessly envied twirling through the air,

—Ah, it finally broke off.

She thought.

※※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※

—When Rem regained consciousness, her feet were not touching the ground.

A sturdy arm was wrapped around her midsection, and she was being carried by someone. The rough, crude handling made it hard to believe they were conscious of touching a woman.

And rightfully so, for the owner of that arm was currently desperate to run, looking as if they didn’t have a shred of leeway to pay attention to anything else.

“—Barusu, right at the broken tree ahead! You’re too slow!”

“Don’t ask… the impossible! Hah, I’m… sprinting at full speed here!”

A familiar voice and a voice she had grown accustomed to hearing were yelling at each other up close.

Being violently jostled up and down, Rem shook her head to bring back her hazy consciousness. And then, her lips trembling,

“…Subaru. What are you…”

“—! You’re awake, Rem!”

Raising a voice of joy while running, Subaru’s face looked down at her.

Looking up at him with hollow eyes, Rem involuntarily choked at the terrible state he was in.

His forehead must have been split open; dripping blood divided his face vertically in crimson. Here and there all over his body, white scars from last night remained, and on top of those, numerous newly acquired wounds were piled up, oozing blood. That was the result of pushing himself recklessly on top of being battered and bruised.

“…Thank goodness, Rem. You really are a handful of a girl.”

Swaying her pink hair, the one faintly smiling while running alongside them was Ram.

She broke her lips into a smile just the tiniest bit, to an extent only someone who knew her well would understand, and gently stroked Rem’s blue hair with her outstretched hand.

Immediately after,

“Fula!”

The chant for a blade of wind was cast, and the swirling wind blades severed the forest—slicing the body of a witchbeast in its path into round slices, turning its leaping form into fertilizer.

In that instant, as if struck by dizziness, Ram’s steps faltered, and she lightly collided with Subaru’s body.

“—Ouuuuchhhhh!! Ram, you, hey… You know my right shoulder is dislocated, right…?!”

“…Shut up. If Ram hadn’t pushed herself, you would’ve been overwritten with curses. Just enjoy being a wall Ram can lean on for a bit.”

“At least use the other shoulder… Owowowowowow!!”

Subaru screamed, half-crying from the intense pain.

Ram’s figure, leaning her weight against his body while bleeding from the “trace of her lost horn.”

Staring at them, Rem suddenly grasped the current situation.

Why she was in a place like this, and why she was being carried by the two of them. It was—

“Why…”

“Huh?”

“Why, didn’t you just leave Rem behind?”

As she was jostled about, that question tumbled out of her mouth.

At Subaru, who looked down at her with a dubious expression, Rem’s lips trembled in quick succession,

“It’s meaningless if Sister, and Subaru came here. Rem has… Rem has to do it alone… It’s enough for only Rem to get hurt…”

“Well, it’s too late for that, Ram and I are completely beat up! We might even be worse off than you!”

Subaru bellowed what was likely the factual truth, without any exaggeration. Ram, perhaps having her own thoughts on the matter, didn’t join the conversation.

Rem felt as if she had been pushed away by her sister’s attitude, and she formed broken words, frantically trying to cling to her.

“It’s Rem’s, it’s Rem’s fault. Because Rem hesitated last night… that’s why Rem has to take responsibility… If not, Rem will never be able to face Sister, or Subaru…”

“Things are pretty rough right now, so could you summarize that for me?! If I get distracted, I’ll seriously end up getting chomped all over in a rerun of last night…”

“If things had gone the way they should have, Subaru wouldn’t have had to get bitten—”

Her voice seemed to reach Subaru clearly, even though he wasn’t in a position to listen.

To him, who stiffened his face and looked at her, Rem confessed her own sin.

During the offense and defense in the forest last night, Rem released the “Oni” inside her and faced the pack of witchbeasts. At that time, her consciousness consisted of the part that surrendered to her instincts as an “Oni,” coexisting with the half of her consciousness that maintained her sense of self.

The severity of the wounds she sustained was terrible, but if she surrendered entirely to instinct, retreating would become difficult.

Her use of a limited “Oni transformation” was based on that judgment. However, it exposed her immature combat skills, and what’s more, it forced Subaru, the one she was supposed to protect, into the choice of throwing himself in harm’s way.

But what Rem truly had to apologize for was not creating that situation.

The moment Subaru protected her and had his entire body devoured by the fangs of the witchbeasts—if things had gone as they should, Rem could have protected him.

Even though she had been shoved aside, the physical strength of an “Oni-transformed” Rem and Subaru’s strength weren’t even comparable. The impact, which had merely caused her to stumble slightly, hadn’t even shifted her from a position where she could reach him if she just turned around and stretched out her arm.

And yet, Rem had hesitated to reach out, causing Subaru to suffer critical, near-fatal injuries.

It was all because of the dense scent drifting from his body—the stench of the day when everything was burned to ashes.

“Because Rem hesitated to reach out to Subaru, Subaru almost died. And he ended up taking far too many curses onto himself. Therefore—”

“So you intended to settle it all by yourself as atonement for that?”

At Rem’s confession, Subaru nodded in understanding, despite his ragged breathing.

As if to affirm his understanding, Rem also tucked her chin, staring at her own sin.

She was prepared to be hurled with abuse, to be despised. Words that normally should have been showered upon her from his mouth before she had ever entered the forest.

Did she delay it because she thought she had to save him as quickly as possible, or was it because she lacked the resolve to face her own weakness? 

—It’s surely the latter,

 Rem thought, mocking her own weak heart.

“Rem.”

“Yes.”

Her name called, she looked up, bracing herself.

No matter what harsh words were thrown at her, she had to accept them willingly.

Because that was the sin she had committed, and the punishment she deserved to be given.

To her,

“Headbutt.”

“—?!”

With a whack, a hard sound of bone striking bone rang out, and sparks flew in Rem’s vision.

Her vision flashed for just a moment from the sharp pain, and Rem pressed a hand to her forehead, unable to understand what just happened. Her current body, not in a “Oni-transformed” state, was not much different in durability from a human’s.

The forehead that received the blow swelled faintly, and from the outside, it was probably red.

Looking down at Rem, whose eyes were darting about in confusion at this incomprehensible situation,

“First off, are you an idiot? No, you’re definitely an idiot.”

“Barusu. Your split forehead split open again and is re-bleeding.”

“I’m an idiot too, I know that! But your sister is an even bigger idiot!”

Saying that to Ram who had interjected, Subaru shook his bleeding head. Seeing that, Rem realized that she had been headbutted by Subaru.

She couldn’t understand what this meant.

“You’re an idiot in many ways, but there are three especially idiotic things. You follow?”

“What are you, saying…”

“First point of idiocy! You saying you couldn’t save me!”

Cutting Rem off while spitting out his words, Subaru hoisted the Rem he was carrying up and brought their faces right together. Widening his dark eyes at a distance where she could feel his breath,

“Wipe your eyes and look real close. Can you see my energetic, manly vigor? Sure, I’ve got a few little white scars left here and there on my body, but scars are a man’s medals, so it’s no problem. Therefore, your feeling of guilt is wrong to begin with, you idiot!”

“But, that’s why, if Rem hadn’t hesitated to begin with, if Rem had reached out my hand right away, you wouldn’t have even suffered such wounds…”

“Yup, stop talking about things in terms of ‘what ifs’! And the second point of idiocy! Trying to shoulder everything and do it all by your lonesome!”

Forcefully silenced, she had no choice but to willingly accept Subaru’s verbal abuse.

She looked to her sister for help, but Ram made no move, as if she intended to observe the situation quietly.

Subaru moved his face toward Rem’s and, sticking his tongue out, said,

“Listen up, in my hometown, there’s a saying: ‘Where three women gather, it’s noisy.’ That has nothing to do with this, but there’s also the saying: ‘Three heads together equal Monju’s wisdom.’”

As he said it, Subaru muttered quietly, “What the heck is a Monju…”, tilted his head, and then said dismissively, “Ah, whatever!”

“Anyway, it’s some story about how three people getting together makes it harder to break arrows than thinking 

alone.”

1

“Rem is just guessing, but she feels like that’s different from how it’s originally used…”

“A-ny-way! Instead of thinking about it alone, lean on the people around you for more things! It’s not like you can’t speak. Unlike me getting my heart squeez—”

Just as he was about to say that, Subaru’s expression suddenly turned bitter.

Naturally hunching forward, breathing painfully to steady himself, Subaru said,

“That’s a foul just from that…? Ain’t the judgment a little too strict?”

“What are you talking about… No, Subaru. Suddenly, the Witch’s scent has become thick…”

Pinching her nose, Rem writhed at the dreadful sensation her olfactory sense was picking up.

Right up close, right beside her, the detestable stench—the lingering scent that was the cause of her hesitation to reach out her hand—was drifting thickly.

Why had it suddenly manifested—

“Well, about that, just move on. I’m moving on too.”

However, Rem’s question was withdrawn by Subaru’s nonchalant tone.

Dumbfounded, Rem stared at Subaru with her mouth hanging open. No emotion beyond his words could be seen on his profile, conveying that he had genuinely postponed the issue.

“And now for the third point of idiocy… crap, we’re out of time.”

Looking ahead while running, Subaru’s gaze narrowed in intense tension.

At the same time, Ram, running beside him, also began deploying her mana while clutching her aching head.

“Ram, in the direction of the village… no, at this point, toward the barrier is fine. Which way do we run to break through?”

“Once we break through the pack in front, it’s a full-speed sprint to the left after that, but what are you planning?”

At Ram’s question, Subaru let out a long groan of “Hmmmm,”

“I shove Rem onto Ram, and mercilessly make my escape all alone far into the barrier—how about that scenario?”

“So you mean becoming a decoy drawing in the ulgarms with the Witch’s scent, while Ram takes Rem and runs away. Got it.”

“Can you stop exposing my tsundere side so easily?!”

Subaru and Ram exchanged this banter without slowing their running pace.

Hearing the conversation between the two of them, Rem voiced her despair with a “That’s…”,

“There’s no way you can survive… Stop, please stop. If you do that, what was Rem…”

“One more point of idiocy added, Rem-rin. This is the best plan for everyone to survive, you know? Once we break through the barrier and somehow regroup, I’ve got a brilliant idea to hunt down all the ulgarms using a method Rem-rin doesn’t know about. That approach will lead to a grand finale, piece of cake, right?”

What this supposed brilliant idea Subaru had prepared was, she didn’t know. To be honest, she even thought it might just be a makeshift lie whose actual existence was doubtful.

Because before that, Subaru breaking through the encirclement single-handedly seemed to Rem like an utterly impossible feat.

“You don’t have to do that… Rem will scatter those witchbeasts…”

Thinking she couldn’t let him do something so reckless, Rem put strength into her entire body.

However, her limply hanging limbs wouldn’t obey her will in the slightest. Her fighting spirit didn’t transmit, and not a single part of her body that would listen to her could be found anywhere.

Her fingertips were trembling. Her facial muscles were the only things she could somewhat move. Her familiar weapon was nowhere to be found in her hands,

“Rem’s, weapon is…”

“I dropped that heavy thing behind! Asking a student with a dislocated arm to carry both you and that is physically impossible, for real!”

And with it clearly stated that she had no weapon, Rem truly knew despair this time.

Just like that, helpless to do anything, Rem’s body was slowly passed over to her sister.

“Don’t drop her.”

“Ram believes she still has more strength than a one-armed Barusu.”

“Then why was I the one carrying Rem?!”

“Because Barusu insisted he would carry her and wouldn’t listen, obviously.”

“No way you gave a serious response!”

Covering his face with his hand, Subaru tried to pretend what he said never happened.

Looking up at such a Subaru, Rem gazed at him as if looking at something unbelievable. Even though she had just voiced how much she had slighted him, why would he go so far…

“Subaru, why go so far…”

“—Let me see.”

At her question, Subaru closed his eyes for just a second, then held up one finger and smiled.

“You’re the first date of my life. I can’t be so heartless as to abandon you.”

Saying that, with the hand holding up the finger, he gently stroked Rem’s hair,

“Well then, I’ll go do this real quick. —Take care of Rem, oneesama.”

“Ram prays that Barusu can safely regroup with us, too.”

Leaving behind that brief exchange, the directions Subaru and Ram were running in rapidly diverged.

Ram went right, Subaru went left. The pack in front of them hesitated for a mere split second over which scattering prey to chase—and instantly set off after Subaru on the left.

“—Sister!”

“It’s the time Barusu put his life on the line to buy. Let’s make effective use of it.”

For her sister, who had lost her Oni powers, the physical strength to support Rem’s body could only be the natural strength her body possessed. Therefore, her running speed was by no means fast.

Feeling that, Rem bit her lip at her own worthlessness.

If only she could “transform into an Oni,” protecting Subaru, or carrying her sister and running in her stead, would be simple. She could do it all.

And yet, when it truly mattered, the “Oni” inside her wouldn’t even attempt to show its face.

Ram’s priority in this situation was solidly locked in as “Rem > Subaru.” So when Subaru presented the method of making himself a decoy, if she judged it would increase their survival rate even a fraction, she could make that decision without hesitation.

While respecting her sister’s decisiveness, Rem couldn’t help but plead through her tears.

Just why, won’t you take it on more boldly?

Just why, won’t you show us more of your amazing side?

Entrusting her with such unreasonableness, just like the total confidence she had in her when she was little, Rem sobbed,

“Subaru… Subaru is…!”

“Don’t look back, Rem. It will leave a scar.”

They were the words of her respected sister. The words of her sister who was always right.

If she obeyed them, her heart would surely be protected. Because she was always, always right.

—If so, being right has no value whatsoever.

“—Big Sister!!”

“—!!”

At the scream that spilled out exactly as her heart demanded, a violent tremor ran across Ram’s expression.

Pressing her lips tight and forcing her eyes open, Ram’s feet came to a halt. Instantly twisting her body to slip out of her sister’s arms, Rem fell to the ground, rolled, and looked behind her.

Far away, a sprint entirely too slow to be called running.

Black hair, covered in wounds, his limp and powerless right arm swaying, Subaru wearing an expression that looked like he was biting back all sorts of emotions rolled into one.

Standing before him was an ulgarm forming a wall with its massive body.

Exceptionally large compared to the rest of its kind, it might have been the boss of the pack.

With such an entity in front of him, and surrounded on his back and sides by countless witchbeasts, Subaru continued running fiercely.

Her hand couldn’t reach that back. Even if she stretched out her fingers, even if her heart trembled, she couldn’t reach.

Even so, Rem just screamed, trying to make it reach.

Praying with all her might that the fingertips that hadn’t reached that night, the feelings that hadn’t reached that night, would reach him this time.

“—Subaru!!”

Whether that voice reached him or not, she didn’t know.

However, as if in answer to that voice—she could just barely see the running Subaru draw a dully gleaming short sword with his left hand.

The roaring of the witchbeast shook the forest.

As if to drown it out her voice, Subaru’s throat also raised in a battle cry.
